question: What is the immediate critical action, regarding fuel, for an in-flight engine fire?

options.text: Turn on the auxiliary fuel transfer pump to drain the hot tank
Cycle the Engine Master switch on and off rapidly
Pull the Emergency Fuel Shutoff Valve fully out to isolate fuel from the engine
Set the power lever to full power to burn off remaining fuel quickly

explanation: Extinguishing an engine-driven fire means cutting off its fuel supply immediately - pulling the Emergency Fuel Shutoff Valve stops all fuel flow from the wing tanks to the engine compartment.

question: What is the correct initial airspeed profile after an engine failure, for a forced landing?

options.text: Maximise speed to 130 KIAS to reach the ground sooner
Slow to 50 KIAS and deploy full landing flap immediately
Maintain best glide speed, clean (flaps up)
Hold 91 KIAS to match the flap limitation speed

explanation: Best glide speed gives the optimum lift-to-drag ratio and therefore the maximum gliding distance to reach a safe landing field, flown with a clean (flaps-up) configuration.

question: What checklist steps are needed to attempt an in-flight engine restart after a flameout?

options.text: Fuel shutoff valve open, Engine Master on, power lever at idle, airspeed within the windmilling envelope
Fuel shutoff valve closed, Electric Master off, flaps at landing
Engine Master off, alternator off, pitch the nose down to spin the engine
Turn on the essential bus switch and wait for the FADEC backup battery to self-start the engine

explanation: A restart attempt needs fuel available (valve open), the engine computers powered (Engine Master on), the power lever at idle to avoid a power surge, and airspeed within the certified windmilling range so airflow can restart core rotation.
